text:
Ana: Quick sync — Nimbus (large fintech pilot) just pushed back. They need a way to buy route-level throughput guarantees (per-customer endpoint) and for that we need a packaging proposal.
Matt: Curious — are they asking for hard limits or priority lanes?
Ana: They want both. Hard cap to prevent noisy tenants + a paid priority lane to guarantee sub-100ms P95.
Jess: Do they want per-route metering in contracts or per-account add-on?
Ana: Per-route. They have multiple endpoints with different SLAs. Legal wants explicit contract language for each route.
Olivia: Heads-up: Dedicated plan can't express per-route billing today. We'd need metering hooks in the console + invoice mapping.
Raj: Implementation note: runtime already supports per-endpoint QoS tokens but we haven't surfaced it to billing. The data pipeline also needs labels for tracing.
Leo: Product ask: define clear launch criteria before we promise Nimbus. Proposal: (1) API + Console UX for route add-on, (2) Billing delta in invoices, (3) Docs + sample contract clause, (4) Canary with <10 customers. Thoughts?
Ana: Agree. Nimbus wants it in 8 weeks though. Is that realistic?
Matt: Eight weeks is tight but doable if we scope: reuse existing QoS token infra, add a small billing mapper, and a minimal console flow. No fancy analytics at launch.
Jess: Risk: legal wants fallback behavior spelled out when capacity constrained. We should include automatic fallback to baseline model and customer credits if SLA violated.
Olivia: Can ops promise the sub-100ms P95 SLA on their infra? That depends on their Dedicated pools. We'll need runbook and an abort/circuit policy.
Raj: Technical checklist (short):
```
- expose route_id in request metadata
- accept qos_token param at request level
- label metrics with route_id + tier
- billing export mapping = route_id -> line item
```
Leo: Launch criteria refinement:
- Beta customers: 3 with production traffic
- Billing: per-route line items appear on invoices for beta accounts
- Reliability: rollback policy + canary for each rollout
- Legal: standard clause template checked off
Ana: Prioritization matrix suggestion:
- Category A (must-have): billing mapper, api flag, minimal console flow, contract template
- Category B (nice-to-have): per-route dashboards, alerting for SLA breach, self-serve escalation
- Category C (later): cross-route quota pooling, predictive autoscale for priority lanes
Matt: Resource ask: one backend eng (4w), one frontend eng (3w), one billing eng (2w), PM + legal time. Parallel tasks ok.
Jess: We should lock scope now. If Nimbus needs full dashboards at launch it adds 6+ weeks.
Ana: I'll push back to Nimbus: aim for beta with must-haves in 8 weeks, dashboards in Q2.
product-bot: Deploy plan template created: https://redwood.internal/plans/route-addon-beta (links in-channel).
Olivia: Ops: I'll draft runbooks and failure mode definitions.
Raj: I'll PR the runtime flags tomorrow.
Leo: OK — action items: Ana to confirm commitment w/ Nimbus; Matt/Jess/Raj to triage tickets; Olivia to start runbooks; Legal to review contract template.
Ana: Thanks — syncing with Nimbus after lunch.
Matt: fyi @Leo we might want to tag this in the roadmap board under "packaging: per-route add-ons"
Leo: done. Added a lightweight epic and linked the action items.
Jess: small reminder — include customer credit calc method in the template (we pre-agreed RTO credits = 1.5x monthly bill for affected route).
Ana: noted. I'll include that in the contract draft.
Olivia: thumbs up :thumbsup:
Leo: Closing thread for now; will reopen if Nimbus pushes.
